chunks: Saʿd narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, from some of our companions, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Dihqān, from Wāṣil ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “There is no salat whose time arrives except that an angel calls out before Allah: O people, rise to the fires which you have kindled upon your backs, then extinguish them with your salat.”

key_terms.أَوْقَدْتُمُوهَا: you have kindled them, meaning you caused them by your deeds
key_terms.بِصَلَاتِكُمْ: by your salat, indicating prayer as the means of purification
key_terms.صَلَاةٍ: salat (prayer), the prescribed act of worship performed at its appointed time
key_terms.فَأَطْفِئُوهَا: then extinguish them, meaning remove and cool their effect
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel who calls people toward prayer
key_terms.نِيرَانِكُمُ: your fires, meaning the spiritual consequences of sins
key_terms.وَقْتُهَا: its designated time, meaning the appointed time for the prayer

ai.seo_question: How does salat (prayer) extinguish sins according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the great spiritual importance of salat (prayer) at its appointed time. It portrays sins as fires kindled by human beings and salat as the means by which those fires are extinguished, highlighting prayer’s purifying and redemptive role.
